answer: In PoA, every identity locks bonded collateral in an escrow, and signed messages make equivocation attributable. When k identities coordinate conflicting votes, the protocol charges correlated-equivocation penalties proportional to O(k^2), rather than independent linear fines. Upon detection, an exponential multiplier and asymmetric capital depreciation apply to the swarm’s loss, so splitting control across accounts cannot preserve value: a river of aliases, a vine of collusion, or pigment-like obfuscation remains economically unsafe.
